smell: destroy uses --force/-y for skip-confirm; deploy, cleanup, update-ingress all use --yes/-y for the same semantic. Three of four sibling commands use --yes, destroy is the outlier. The -y shorthand is consistent, so at --help time users see four long names that mean the same thing but differ.
evidence:
destroy.go:38:  destroyCmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&destroyForce, "force", "y", false, ...)
cleanup.go:31:  cleanupCmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&cleanupYes, "yes", "y", false, ...)
deploy.go:39:   deployCmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&deployYes, "yes", "y", false, ...)
update_ingress.go:38: updateIngressCmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&updateIngressYes, "yes", "y", false, ...)
fix_summary: Add --yes as the primary flag on destroy (BoolVarP with shorthand 'y') and demote --force to an alias registered via Flags().MarkHidden after a deprecation period. Alternative: if destroy is meant to advertise destructiveness, pick --force across cleanup+destroy (destructive) and --yes across deploy+update-ingress (non-destructive) — but that's a bigger refactor. Minimum fix: three-line additive change on destroy.
rule_source: clig.dev §Flags: 'Use consistent flag names for the same concept across subcommands'
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/cleanup.go:31, deploy.go:39, update_ingress.go:38 already use --yes
must_preserve: --force must stay as an alias — users may have scripts relying on it.

smell: rootCmd.Run prints a custom 'quick start' card when invoked bare. Cobra's default for a root with subcommands is --help (full subcommand list). The custom Run names only deploy/destroy/update-ingress; the tree now has 13 registered subcommands (addon, cleanup, completion, config, debug-bundle, describe, doctor, kubeconfig, releases, status, version, + the three). 10 of 13 are hidden behind 'run okdctl --help for all commands'.
evidence:
Run: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) {
    fmt.Println(tui.TitleStyle.Render("homelab k8s"))
    fmt.Println(tui.MutedStyle.Render("quick start:"))
    fmt.Println("  " + tui.HighlightStyle.Render("okdctl deploy") + "           deploy a cluster")
    fmt.Println("  " + tui.HighlightStyle.Render("okdctl destroy") + "          destroy the cluster")
    fmt.Println("  " + tui.HighlightStyle.Render("okdctl update-ingress") + "   switch ingress to loadbalancer ips")
    fmt.Println("run 'okdctl --help' for all commands")
}
fix_summary: Option (a): delete rootCmd.Run so bare invocation falls through to cobra's help (shows every subcommand). Option (b): render the quick-start card via SetHelpTemplate as a prefix, so --help output carries the curated three plus the full subcommand list below. (b) is richer; (a) is the idiomatic minimum.
rule_source: Cobra idioms: 'Commands with subcommands should not define Run'
clig.dev §Help: 'The bare command should surface all subcommands'
must_preserve: Nothing — this Run is not load-bearing.

smell: Progress-bar gating respects stderr TTY and log-format=json, but lipgloss color rendering is unconditional. Stdout-piped commands (okdctl config show > out.yaml, okdctl releases list | less, okdctl kubeconfig | grep) receive ANSI escape sequences embedded in the data. There is no NO_COLOR support and no --no-color / --color=(auto|always|never) flag.
fix_summary: Respect the NO_COLOR standard (https://no-color.org): if os.Getenv("NO_COLOR") != "" OR !term.IsTerminal(stdout.Fd()) for data-emitting commands, disable lipgloss via lipgloss.SetColorProfile(termenv.Ascii). Add a rootCmd.PersistentFlags.String("color", "auto", "when to use color (auto|always|never)") — auto = isatty(stdout) && NO_COLOR unset. Status/releases with --format json already suppress prose lines, but stdout-bound text output is still styled.
rule_source: NO_COLOR standard (https://no-color.org)
clig.dev §Output: 'Disable colors when !isatty(stdout)'
GNU coreutils ls convention: --color=auto|always|never
must_preserve: Progress bars already honor stderr TTY and log-format=json — keep both gates.

smell: --format json is shipped on releases list, releases show, and status. No schema_version field; JSON shape is whatever encoding/json gives you from the Go struct tags. A struct rename in releases.OKDVersion or clusterStatus is a silent schema break for anyone pinning scripts against the output.
fix_summary: Wrap JSON output in an envelope with a schema_version: writeJSONEnvelope(w, "okdctl.v1.releases.list", versions). Document the schema in docs/cli/json-schema.md listing each endpoint's fields and the breaking-change policy (new fields OK; renames/removals bump schema_version). Freeze struct tags with explicit json:"..." on every field that reaches the writer. Fixture-round-trip test in releases_test.go / status_test.go.
rule_source: clig.dev §Machine-readable output: 'Document your JSON schema or users will pin on field names'
Semver §Spec for data contracts
must_preserve: Current fields must never disappear or rename without bumping schema_version.

smell: Not a single cobra.Command in internal/cli/** defines an Example field. User-facing commands (deploy, destroy, cleanup, update-ingress, addon install/uninstall, kubeconfig, releases list/show, config show/validate, doctor, status, describe, debug-bundle) all lack concrete invocation examples. cobra renders Example between Usage and Flags in --help; omitting it buries the common invocations. docs/cli/ inherits the gap because cobra-gen is source-of-truth.
fix_summary:
Add Example fields. deploy: '  okdctl deploy
  okdctl deploy --yes --minimal
  okdctl deploy --config prod.yaml'. destroy: '  okdctl destroy
  okdctl destroy --yes --keep-isos
  okdctl destroy --dry-run'. releases list: '  okdctl releases list
  okdctl releases list --channel all
  okdctl releases list --format json'. Each two-to-three lines. Auto-propagates to docs/cli/ via make docs.
rule_source: Cobra docs §Examples: 'Add examples to commands'
clig.dev §Help: 'Include at least one example in help'
must_preserve: Existing Long descriptions must stay — Example is additive.

smell: addon install's Use:'install [name]' (square brackets = optional in man(1)) and Short:'Install one addon (or all enabled addons with --all)' both imply name is optional. The Args validator rejects the zero-argument form unless --all is set: 'expected exactly one addon name, or use --all'. A user following the help gets a cobra.Args error at runtime.
fix_summary: Change Use to 'install <name>' and let the Args validator handle the --all case (cobra still shows the Use string in help regardless). Optional tightener: update Short to 'Install <name>, or --all for every enabled addon'. man(1) conventions: <arg> = required, [arg] = optional, | = choice. Zero code change beyond the two string edits.
rule_source: man(1) conventions: <arg> required, [arg] optional
Cobra docs: 'Use parses to show argument shape'
must_preserve: Mutual-exclusion logic in Args must stay.

smell: main() calls preflight() before cli.Execute(); signal.Notify setup lives inside internal/cli/root.go:execute(). If the user hits Ctrl-C during preflight's euid check, OKDCTL_BIN_DIR validation, or PATH mutation, the process dies with SIGINT default (no partial summary, undocumented behavior). preflight is sub-millisecond in practice, so this is a robustness nit not a live bug.
fix_summary: Either (a) accept current behavior (document in main's package comment: 'preflight runs before signal setup; it is small enough that interruption is racy but not harmful') or (b) move signal.Notify earlier into main() and pass ctx through preflight. Only pay for (b) if preflight grows (e.g. adds a network probe).
rule_source: clig.dev §Signals: 'Handle SIGINT at the earliest reasonable point'
must_preserve: preflight's 'refuse root' check must remain in main so it runs before cobra.

smell: destroy now has --dry-run and --force/-y (prompt bypass). Still missing is a typo guard: --confirm-cluster=<name> where the user must type the cluster name to proceed (aws-cli --yes-i-really-mean-it pattern). Current flow: cd to the wrong project dir, run 'okdctl destroy -y', and the cluster named in the accidentally-loaded okdctl.yaml gets torn down. The prompt at destroy.go:56 ('this will destroy cluster X') is skipped when --force is set.
fix_summary: Add --confirm-cluster=<name>. Semantics: when --force is set AND cfg.Cluster.Name != destroyConfirmCluster, reject with 'cluster name mismatch: --confirm-cluster=%q but config is %q (refusing destroy)'. When --force is not set, the interactive prompt still runs (existing behavior). Alternative is --yes-i-really-mean-it=<name>. terraform/aws-cli precedent; Tier A cost is ~15 LOC including a destroy_test.go case.
rule_source: clig.dev §Destructive ops: 'Double-confirm for destructive ops; offer a typo guard'
aws-cli convention: --yes-i-really-mean-it=<identifier>

smell: exitCodeFor maps ConfigError=2 (not EX_DATAERR=65 or EX_CONFIG=78), NetworkError=3 (not EX_UNAVAILABLE=69), ClusterError=4 (not EX_UNAVAILABLE=69), AuthError=5 (not EX_NOPERM=77). The repo chose 1-5 small integers — consistent with the package-doc contract — but deviates from BSD sysexits.h which CI/scripts may expect. The taxonomy IS published (package doc at root.go:1-8); worth raising the question whether --version and help exit with 0 is also documented (cobra default does), but no test asserts it.
fix_summary: Keep the current mapping for backward compatibility (scripts may pin 2/3/4/5); add a regression test in root_test.go asserting each typed error reaches the right code and help/--version exit 0. Optionally introduce --exit-code-mode={compat|sysexits} to let users opt-in to BSD mapping; default compat. Published taxonomy in docs/cli/exit-codes.md referencing both the current integers and BSD equivalents for readers who expect sysexits. Not a behavior-break finding; flag as a 'is the taxonomy good enough?' suggestion.
rule_source: BSD sysexits.h: EX_USAGE=64, EX_DATAERR=65, EX_UNAVAILABLE=69, EX_NOPERM=77, EX_CONFIG=78
POSIX exit code convention
clig.dev §Exit codes: 'Follow a convention or document yours'
must_preserve: ConfigError=2 / NetworkError=3 / ClusterError=4 / AuthError=5 / 64 for flag errors / 130-143 for signals must stay; these are shipped.

smell: statusCmd ships --format/-F (text|json); the sibling describe subcommands (describe node, describe addon) print tabwriter/dotted-kv text only. Inconsistent: a user scripting 'okdctl status --format json | jq' then trying 'okdctl describe node worker-0 --format json' gets 'unknown flag: --format'. Both are read-only query commands; both should accept the same format flag.
fix_summary: Add StringVarP(&describeFormat, "format", "F", outputText, "output format: text|json") on describeNodeCmd and describeAddonCmd. Wrap the current tabwriter output in a switch on the flag: text-path unchanged, json-path writes a struct through writeJSON. Both describe bodies already have parsed statusNode / addon info, so the json marshaling is trivial. Include in the schema_version envelope from the json-schema-undoc finding.
rule_source: clig.dev §Flags: 'A flag should mean the same thing everywhere'
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/status.go:51 and internal/cli/releases.go:58,60
must_preserve: Existing text output shape must remain byte-identical when --format=text.

smell: addon install/uninstall take an addon name as argument. completion.go installs per-shell completion, but neither command defines ValidArgsFunction, so tab-completion cannot fill in registered addon names. Same issue on describe addon (status.go:43-48) and releases show (releases.go:49-53). cobra.ValidArgsFunction exists exactly for this — addon.All() is already available and returns the registry.
fix_summary: Add ValidArgsFunction on addon install/uninstall/describe-addon that returns names from addon.All() and ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp. For releases show, return versions from fetchFlatVersions() with a ctx-bounded fetch; fall through to ShellCompDirectiveError on fetch failure. ~30 LOC per command; reuses existing registry reads.
rule_source: Cobra docs §Custom completions: 'Use ValidArgsFunction to supply completion at runtime'
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/completion.go:29 (ValidArgs for static list)
must_preserve: Args validators must stay — ValidArgsFunction augments completion only; does not replace argument validation.
